input: words is an Array of W lowercase ASCII strings, 0 <= W <= 1000, each with length in [1,16]. Duplicate strings are permitted; the empty outer Array is an explicit extension. Integer inputs are primitive safe-integer Numbers, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays without holes, subclasses, proxies or accessors; strings are primitive. No concurrent mutation or modified standard built-ins are allowed. Preconditions are not dynamically validated. Size bounds do not guarantee available memory or completion within an unqualified runtime budget.
return: The greatest number of words in a chain where each next word is obtained by inserting exactly one letter anywhere into the previous word, preserving its existing letter order. Return 0 for no words. Equal duplicates do not extend a chain.
mutation_aliasing: Only a fresh outer ordering is sorted by word length; caller ordering and immutable word values remain unchanged. A private map retains the maximum chain ending at each word. Predecessor deletion strings are temporary and no result chain or mutable input alias is returned. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: Lengths and comparator differences are within [1,16] and [-15,15]. Every chain length is at most 16 since each step adds one character. Prefix/suffix slice boundaries and all counters are exact; ASCII semantics align Python and JavaScript indexing.
complexity: Let L<=16 be maximum word length. Beyond sorting, O(W*L^2+W+1) expected work includes constructing, concatenating, hashing and comparing all deletion strings; deletion is not treated as free. O(W+L+1) live map/reference and transient-string storage beyond sort workspace; total transient character allocation is O(W*L^2). JavaScript copied sorting adds O(W+1) copying plus target-runtime T_sort(W) comparison/sort work and S_sort(W) workspace. ECMAScript supplies no universal O(W log W) sort complexity guarantee; comparator work is bounded O(1) here and is included in T_sort. Map/set costs assume ordinary average O(1) operations after charging key construction/hash/comparison; no universal ECMAScript constant-time or adversarial collision-resistance guarantee is claimed.
